sentences.text: Alberta reported that occupational exposures account for approximately 8% of cancer cases in the population, though among those exposed to occupational carcinogens, the proportion of cancer attributable to these exposures is likely greater.

Alberta noted that occupational carcinogens can be chemical (such as benzene), physical (such as ionizing radiation), or biological (such as Hepatitis C) in nature, and can enter the body through inhalation, absorption through the skin, ingestion with food, or direct exposure to radiation.
The Alberta Cancer Board maintains a cancer registry that records new cases of cancer among residents of the province, though workplace information is not routinely collected.
